skeleton: little girl standing, front three-quarter view: root at the feet; body (swimsuit torso, pivot at the hips) with belly squash; head at the neck (hat, hair and bunches on it), face with eyes, brows, nose and mouth (each eye its own piece, both looking the same way); two-segment arms: armL/armR at the shoulders (upper arms tucked behind the body's rounded shoulders) and elbowL/elbowR (forearms with hands laid over the upper arms with faded tops: relaxed, fist, waving, pointing, clapping); armL (the viewer's left, her right) rests folded with the hand on her chest; two-segment legs: legL/legR at the hips (thighs under the swimsuit's frill) and kneeL/kneeR (lower legs with feet over the thighs, faded tops; in a squat both come up in front of her tummy, knees high, on the front slots); the kite with its string on its own bone at the armL fist; a sand heap on the root for play-sand.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a little girl holding a kite on a string. Draw this exact girl as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: her torso in the blue polka-dot swimsuit with its ruffled frill at the hips, as in image 1, with her bare shoulders and neck, without head, without arms and without legs: no arms and no hands drawn on it, no legs below the frill; the top of the neck, normally under the head, rounded.
2. the head: her head with the yellow sun hat, its red ribbon and bow, her brown hair with its two bunches and little red hair ties, and her ears, turned as in image 1, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no eyebrows, no nose, no mouth — keep the rosy cheeks; its bottom edge, at the chin and the neck, rounded.
3. the kite arm: her arm on the left of image 1, drawn whole from the top of the shoulder down to the hand, bent at the elbow with the hand raised beside her as in image 1, the hand a loose fist (with no string in it); its top the full, smooth, rounded curve of the shoulder.
4. the same arm hanging down straight and relaxed beside her, with its open hand; its top the same rounded shoulder.
5. the free arm: her arm on the right of image 1, drawn whole from the top of the shoulder down to the open hand, hanging relaxed as in image 1; its top the full, smooth, rounded curve of the shoulder.
6. the same free arm raised up high, bent a little at the elbow, the open hand up with its fingers spread, waving; its rounded shoulder at the bottom.
7. the same free arm held out straight, the hand pointing with its index finger; its rounded shoulder at one end.
8. her left leg (on the left of image 1), drawn whole from the top of the thigh, normally hidden under the frill, down to the bare foot, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded curve.
9. her right leg (on the right of image 1), drawn whole from the top of the thigh down to the bare foot, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded curve.
10. the kite on its string: the colourful diamond kite with its ribbon tail of three little bows and its thin string running down from the kite, all as in image 1, just the kite, its tail and its string, no hand.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a little girl; image 2 shows the same girl cut into puppet parts. Draw her arms and legs again as cut-out puppet parts with real joints, so the puppet can bend at the elbows and knees: each arm in two pieces (the upper arm; the forearm with its hand) and each leg in two pieces (the thigh; the lower leg with its foot). The same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every piece at the size and thickness it has on the girl in image 1: soft, chubby little-girl arms and legs, as thick as in image 1, never thin or stick-like.

Draw each piece on its own, every piece hanging straight down, spread out over the sheet in two tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, no piece touching or overlapping another:
1. her upper arm: from the top of her bare shoulder, a full rounded cap, straight down to the elbow; both ends full and rounded.
2. her forearm with the hand open and relaxed, fingers together, as her hanging hand is in image 1: from a full rounded elbow end down to the fingertips.
3. her forearm with the hand closed in a loose fist, as if holding a string: from a full rounded elbow end down to the fist.
4. her forearm with the hand open, palm towards the viewer, fingers spread, as when waving: from a full rounded elbow end, the hand at the bottom.
5. her forearm with the hand pointing with its index finger, the finger pointing straight down: from a full rounded elbow end.
6. her forearm with the hand flat and seen from its side, thumb on top, fingers together, as when clapping: from a full rounded elbow end.
7. her thigh: from the top of the thigh, normally hidden under the swimsuit's frill, a full rounded curve, straight down to the knee; the knee end full and rounded.
8. her lower leg with its bare foot: from a full rounded knee end straight down to the ankle, the foot flat, its toes pointing to the left as her left foot is in image 1.

Every piece is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and every joint end is a full, smooth, rounded edge with the drawing's line all round it. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the pieces beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a little girl; image 2 shows the same girl cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the girl's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the girl in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. In image 1 both her eyes look up and to the left: each dark iris sits towards the left of its eye, the white on its right.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the eye on the LEFT of image 1, six times, its little lashes at its outer (left) corner:
1. as it is in image 1: a big dark round iris with a white sparkle, looking up and to the left.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, looking the same way, with its white sparkle.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U.
4. sad: looking down and to the left, its upper lid drooping, a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in a blink: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye.
Row 2, the eye on the RIGHT of image 1, the same six in the same order, its lashes at its outer (right) corner; open, it looks the same way as row 1, up and to the left, the iris towards the left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. her eyebrow as it is in image 1, a thin brown arch. 14. the same eyebrow sad, tilted up at one end. 15. her small nose as it is in image 1.
Row 4: 16. her mouth as it is in image 1, a happy closed smile. 17. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, the inside pink. 18. the mouth open in a small round 'o'. 19. the mouth in a small sad frown. 20. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a little girl flying a kite; image 2 shows the same girl and kite cut into puppet parts. Draw two more cut-out puppet parts on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours, texture and line as in the images, each at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, far apart on the sheet, nothing touching:
1. the kite alone: the same colourful diamond kite with its ribbon tail of little bows, exactly as in image 1, WITHOUT any string.
2. the kite string alone: one long, thin, perfectly straight dark-brown line, standing upright, about two thirds as tall as the sheet, nothing else on it.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a little girl; image 2 shows the same girl cut into puppet parts. Draw more cut-out puppet parts of this exact girl on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in images 1 and 2, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. her near arm (on the left of image 1) as it is in image 1: drawn whole from the top of the shoulder down to the hand, bent at the elbow, the empty hand resting relaxed on her chest; its top the full, smooth, rounded curve of the shoulder.
2. one arm reaching straight down and a little forward to the ground, drawn whole from the top of the shoulder to the open hand, its palm flat facing down as if patting sand; its top the full rounded curve of the shoulder.
3. her two legs in a deep squat, crouching low on her heels, drawn together as one piece seen from the front as in image 1: knees bent up and apart, thighs folded down onto her calves, both bare feet flat on the ground; from the tops of the thighs (normally hidden under the swimsuit's frill) down to the feet; the tops of the thighs one smooth rounded edge. Low and wide: from the tops of the thighs to the soles, about a third as tall as her standing legs.
4. a small heap of golden beach sand, a soft rounded mound with a few grains around its foot, about as wide as her two hands.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.
